newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN says airlift to east Zaire refugees within days.
newsitem.headline: UN says airlift to east Zaire refugees within days.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency said on Tuesday that it would start airlifting relief supplies within days to hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees fleeing Tutsi rebels in eastern Zaire.
Spokeswoman Ruth Marshall told reporters that supplies would be flown from Zaire's capital Kinshasa to Kisangani to reach refugees out of contact since fighting broke out three weeks ago.

The move came as Canada said it was ready to command a multinational force in Zaire to ease the way for relief supplies. South Africa had also agreed to take part, U.N. Secretary-General Boutros-Boutros Ghali said in Rome.

Marshall, of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), said airlifted supplies would be trucked to the refugees from Kisangani, last outpost of tenuous Zairean authority before a wilderness of forest and hills.
The town is 500 km (310 miles) from eastern Zaire's volatile border region of Goma.
More than half a million mostly Rwandan Hutu refugees fled their camps outside Rwanda's borders after Rwandan-backed Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels seized large swathes of eastern Zaire.
"We're trying from every direction so that we can to get aid effectively and quickly to all the people in need -- refugees and displaced Zaireans," said Marshall.

The United Nations said in Geneva that 40 tonnes of high energy biscuits had been airlifted to Uganda's capital Kampala. Another 100 tonnes of relief supplies would be flown to Kinshasa from Denmark on Wednesday on board a Russian Antonov 124 plane.
Marshall said the UNHCR had no evidence of a mass exodus of refugees from eastern Zaire's Goma region on Rwanda's northwestern border to Kisangani.

The main road from Goma and Bukavu to Kisangani was used as a line of retreat for troops from the battlefront. Recent aid flights over the area have revealed few people on the road, but also that the villages were deserted.
A symbolic amount of food, medical supplies and blankets trucked into Goma by U.N. and independent aid agencies on Monday -- the first aid to reach eastern Zaire from Rwanda since April last year.

In Kinshasa, Zairean Information Minister Boguo Makele told Reuters Zaire had no objection to aid arriving in the country via the capital and being distributed to displaced Zaireans. But he denounced aid taken into Goma from Rwanda.
"This constitutes a violation of our territorial integrity," he said. "Aid for the (Rwanda) refugees should be distributed in Rwanda."
